summary:
SPHEREx Sky Navigator is an interactive, browser-based astronomical tool built to analyze multi-epoch near-infrared observations from NASA's SPHEREx space telescope. Because the raw SPHEREx FITS images arrive with rotated orientations, zodiacal background glow, and in 102 spectral channels, spotting faint moving objects like distant trans-Neptunian candidates, asteroids, or high-proper-motion brown dwarfs becomes challenging without any tools or specialized pipelines. 

Our application's goal is to make the process easier and enjoyable, by integrating several features, like automatic zodiacal light subtraction, aligning of exposures, custom blink rates, custom subtraction of epochs to isolate motion dipoles, and coadding of all six detector arrays to generate the 102-band infrared spectra on the fly. Moreover, the UI offers several customization features, allowing for a better user experience. By integrating live NASA IRSA queries, ESA Gaia DR3 and AllWISE catalog overlays, shareable deep URLs, and pre-cached benchmark targets (WISE 0855, Barnard's Star), our tool empowers both researchers and citizen scientists to accelerate discoveries across every new SPHEREx data release.
details:
Overview & How It Works

SPHEREx Sky Navigator is an end-to-end Python web application that connects directly to the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) via Table Access Protocol (TAP) and Simple Image Access (SIA) queries (spherex_dr1 and spherex_qr3 releases). When a user selects one of NASA’s five benchmark targets (WISE 0855, Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi B, RW Aurigae, R Draconis) or enters custom celestial coordinates, our pipeline automatically subtracts the ZODI (zodiacal light) extension from each raw IMAGE FITS frame and reprojects every exposure onto a locked North-Up World Coordinate System (WCS) tangent grid (6.2"/pixel). This eliminates spacecraft roll-angle rotation so stationary background stars remain fixed while moving objects visibly jump across epochs.

Core Scientific & Discovery Capabilities

  • Time-Series Blink Comparator: Offers both an animated auto-loop player and manual frame stepper with ZScale dynamic contrast stretching, Astrometrica negative inversion, bilinear/nearest-neighbor pixel interpolation, adjustable Field of View (2–25 arcmin), and fullscreen inspection.
  • Epoch Addition & Subtraction: Lets users subtract any baseline frame from a comparison frame (Epoch B − Epoch A) so static stars cancel out into clean positive/negative motion dipoles, or coadd epochs (Epoch A + Epoch B) to boost signal-to-noise for faint targets.
  • 102-Band Spectral & Detector Array Explorer: Measures aperture photometry across all six SPHEREx detector arrays (0.75–5.00 µm), generates an interpolated 102-channel infrared spectral profile on the fly, coadds exposures within individual detector bands to reveal cold thermal emission or ice absorption features, and plots MJD photometric light curves for variable stars.
  • Multi-Catalog Cross-Matching & Deep URLs: Overlays live ESA Gaia DR3 optical stars and NASA AllWISE infrared sources via VizieR so any uncircled moving source stands out immediately, while syncing ?ra=...&dec=...&fov=... parameters in the browser URL for instant bookmarking and embedding.

Tech Stack, Creativity & Design Considerations

Built in Python using Streamlit, Astropy (WCS, SkyCoord, ZScaleInterval, Cutout2D), Astroquery, Reproject, NumPy, Pandas, and Matplotlib, our architecture balances live cloud queries with pre-cached .npz benchmark cubes and automatic TAP-to-SIA server failover for zero-latency exploration. Users can also save custom sky bookmarks, customize UI themes and DPI resolution, and export observation logs (.md), metadata tables (.csv), FITS-derived image stacks (.npz), and publication-ready PNG frames. By turning complex orbital spectroscopy into an intuitive browser workflow, SPHEREx Sky Navigator empowers both astronomers and citizen scientists to accelerate discoveries across every upcoming SPHEREx data release.

AI Assistance Disclosure

During development, our team used AI-assisted coding and drafting tools to help debug Astropy/Astroquery API queries, refine Streamlit UI layout styling, and polish our project documentation and video pitch script. All scientific logic, astronomical data pipelines, benchmark validation, and application architecture were designed, tested, and verified by Team Meridian IR.
